newsitem.title: USA: Former Texaco executive pleads innocent.
newsitem.headline: Former Texaco executive pleads innocent.

text.p: A former Texaco Inc. executive pleaded innocent Wednesday to obstruction of justice in connection with a separate race discrimination suit, the U.S. Attorney's office said.

A spokesman for the Manhattan U.S. Attorney's office said the former executive, Richard Lundwall, pleaded not guilty to the charge before U.S. Magistrate Judge Mark Fox in White Plains, N.Y., Federal Court.
The case was assigned to U.S. District Judge Barrington Parker, but no date for the trial has been set.

Lundwall, 55, former senior coordinator of personnel services of Texaco's finance department, was first charged in November with obstruction of justice through a complaint filed by the Manhattan U.S. Attorney's Office.
The case against Lundwall stems from his decision to come forward with evidence against himself and others in the discrimination case against Texaco.
In that class action suit, filed in 1994, a group of black employees alleged that Texaco discriminated against them in promotions and pay.

Lundwall had secretly taped conversations between himself and others in which they discussed destroying documents requested by the plaintiffs. When Lundwall was dismissed by Texaco in a downsizing move last summer, he gave the tapes to the plaintiffs' lawyers.
After the tapes were made public in court proceedings, Texaco agreed to settle the case for $176.1 million.
If convicted, Lundwall could face a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
